canonical_name: Weak perfect graph theorem family (finite-simple-graph reading is a source lead, not yet frozen)
literal_source_claim_zh: 图的完美性与其补图的完美性等价
literal_source_claim_en: The perfectness of a graph is equivalent to the perfectness of its complement.
source_attribution: Laszlo Lovasz, 1972 (catalog metadata; two direct primary-source leads identified)
statement_blocker: The catalog does not define a perfect graph or state finiteness and graph-model assumptions. It omits the all-induced-subgraphs quantifier, chromatic and clique-number conventions, subset/subtype encoding, same-carrier complement transport, ordered binders, and degenerate cases. The two identified 1972 primary texts were not fully inspected or independently reviewed. Selecting an exact proposition at intake would invent source clauses.
target_decision: retain a planned weak-perfect-graph-theorem instance and require an independently reviewed primary-source proposition before statement execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix a finite simple undirected loopless graph on a vertex type V : Type u (or another exact model), its Fintype/Finite and decidability assumptions, and the universe and subtype conventions for induced graphs.
conclusion: Open: for the source-defined perfectness predicate, a graph is perfect if and only if its same-carrier complement is perfect; the exact induced-subgraph, clique, chromatic, coercion, and finite-value encoding is unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: for every finite simple graph G, Perfect G if and only if Perfect G complement
the one-way complement implication plus complement involution
perfectness defined by chromatic-number equals clique-number for every induced vertex subset
Lovasz's normal-hypergraph min-max route to the complement theorem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty and singleton induced vertex subsets
zero clique and chromatic numbers and Nat-to-ENat coercions
isolated and universal vertices and disconnected graphs
complement and induce order on subtype carriers
finite carrier as a typeclass premise versus explicit finite vertex set
excluded_substitutions: the strong perfect graph theorem or an odd-hole and antihole characterization
chromatic number equals clique number only for the ambient graph
a perfect matching, chordal, comparability, bipartite, weighted, directed, multigraph, infinite-graph, or hypergraph theorem
the replication lemma, stable-set inequality, normal-hypergraph duality, or complement involution alone
a predicate, structure, or hypothesis storing the desired equivalence
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe used as proof credit
